dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real m-by-n matrix A and real numbers lower and upper, this is the conjunction (for every x in R^n, lower * ||x||_2 <= ||Ax||_2) and (for every x in R^n, ||Ax||_2 <= upper * ||x||_2).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the two-sided norm-bound predicates compared in the conclusion: bounds [α, β] for QA*T and bounds [β^{-1}, α^{-1}] for C.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real m-by-n matrix Q, this asserts that ||Qx||_2 = ||x||_2 for every x in R^n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The hypotheses require both QA and Q to preserve the Euclidean norm exactly.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is matrix-vector multiplication: for A of size m-by-n and x in R^n, (Ax)_i = sum over j in Fin n of A_{ij} x_j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies every matrix action occurring in norm preservation and norm bounds, and the induced map x maps to Tx whose surjectivity is assumed.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is matrix multiplication: for A of size m-by-n and B of size n-by-p, (AB)_{ij} = sum over k in Fin n of A_{ik} B_{kj}.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms QA*T in the left-hand norm bounds and C*T in the hypothesis C*T = Q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a matrix A and scalar c, this asserts the lower norm bound c * ||x||_2 <= ||Ax||_2 for every vector x in the domain.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the lower bounds α for QA*T and β^{-1} for C.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a matrix A and scalar c, this asserts the upper norm bound ||Ax||_2 <= c * ||x||_2 for every vector x in the domain.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the upper bounds β for QA*T and α^{-1} for C.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x in R^n, this is the Euclidean norm ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of x_i^2).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes every norm in the hypotheses and conclusion to be the finite-dimensional Euclidean norm.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction: both component propositions must hold.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines each lower and upper bound, and also requires both the bound equivalence and the ratio equality in the final conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the division operation from a DivInvMonoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to the real-number structure, it supplies ordinary real division for the two displayed ratios.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality of two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses norm preservation, matrix equality C*T = Q, the preimage equation in surjectivity, and the concluding equality of ratios.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type with elements corresponding to 0, 1, ..., n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes all matrix rows, matrix columns, vectors, and finite sums, thereby fixing their dimensions.

dependency_coverage.name: Function.Surjective
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function f is surjective when for every target value b there exists a source value a, depending on b, such that f(a) = b.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The hypothesis says that for every y in R^n there exists x in R^n such that Tx = y.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the heterogeneous division operation supplied by an HDiv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real arguments and the real division instance, it interprets β/α and α^{-1}/β^{-1} as real quotients.

dependency_coverage.name: Iff
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical equivalence: each of the two propositions implies the other.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It states that the specified two-sided bounds for QA*T hold exactly when the reciprocal, order-reversed bounds for C hold.

dependency_coverage.name: Inv.inv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the unary inverse operation supplied by an Inv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real instance, it produces β^{-1} and α^{-1} in the bounds and ratio identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the strict-order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real strict order, it expresses the hypotheses 0 < α and 0 < β.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The dimensions m, n, and s are arbitrary natural numbers, so zero-dimensional cases are included.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets a natural-number literal in a type using its OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 0 in the positivity hypotheses as the real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All matrix entries, vector coordinates, bounds, norms, inverses, and quotients are real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard multiplication, reciprocal, division satisfying a/b = a*b^{-1}, and integer-power operations.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real division structure used to interpret the quotient expressions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instInv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard reciprocal operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets α^{-1} and β^{-1}; positivity ensures both inputs are nonzero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard strict order <.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the assumptions on α and β ordinary strict positivity.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with the standard element 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the zero appearing in 0 < α and 0 < β.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructs the interpretation of the numeral 0 from a type's distinguished zero element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the numeral in the positivity hypotheses denotes real zero.

dependency_coverage.name: instHDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns a homogeneous division operation on a type into an HDiv operation with the same input and output type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It exposes standard real division to the notation used by both quotient expressions.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This gives Fin n its canonical finite enumeration.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits sums over every coordinate in Fin n and the construction of the full finite index set.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This sums the values of a function over a finite set using the additive commutative monoid operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It computes matrix-vector products, matrix products, and sums of coordinate squares.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the finite set containing every element of a finite type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Fin n it makes each displayed sum range over all coordinates or contracted matrix indices.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the heterogeneous multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real arguments, it gives ordinary real multiplication in matrix products, matrix-vector products, scalar norm bounds, and coordinate squares indirectly through powers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard additive commutative monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies real addition and zero for all finite sums defining products and norms.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with standard multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies multiplication of matrix entries and vector coordinates and multiplication of scalar bounds by norms.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns a homogeneous multiplication operation into an HMul operation with the same input and output type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It exposes standard real multiplication to all products used in the local definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the exponentiation operation supplied by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets each x_i^2 in the Euclidean norm definition.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets all lower and upper norm bounds as ordinary non-strict real inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips a monoid with natural-number exponentiation by repeated multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the real multiplicative monoid, it makes exponent 2 denote the ordinary square of each coordinate.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard non-strict order <=.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the order relation in every norm inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their standard multiplicative monoid structure, including multiplication, one, and natural powers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the natural-power operation used to square vector coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the nonnegative real square-root function; in the target it is applied only to nonnegative sums of squares.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns each sum of coordinate squares into the Euclidean norm.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns a power operation with a given exponent type into the corresponding HPow operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It exposes natural-number powers of real numbers to the expression x_i^2.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets each natural-number numeral as that natural number itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the exponent literal 2 as the natural number two.

binders: m, n, and s are arbitrary natural-number dimensions.
QA is an m-by-n real matrix, represented as a function Fin m -> Fin n -> Real.
Q and C are s-by-n real matrices.
T is an n-by-n real matrix.
α and β are real numbers.
hypotheses: QA preserves the Euclidean norm: for every x in R^n, ||QA x||_2 = ||x||_2.
Q preserves the Euclidean norm: for every x in R^n, ||Qx||_2 = ||x||_2.
The exact matrix equality C*T = Q holds.
The map induced by T is surjective: for every y in R^n, there exists an x in R^n, depending on y, such that Tx = y.
conclusions: The following statements are logically equivalent: (i) for every x in R^n, α||x||_2 <= ||(QA*T)x||_2 and ||(QA*T)x||_2 <= β||x||_2; (ii) for every x in R^n, β^{-1}||x||_2 <= ||Cx||_2 and ||Cx||_2 <= α^{-1}||x||_2.
The exact real-number equality β/α = α^{-1}/β^{-1} holds.
mathematical_definitions: For x in R^n, ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i^2).
For an m-by-n matrix A, (Ax)_i = sum_{j=0}^{n-1} A_{ij}x_j.
For compatible matrices A and B, (AB)_{ij} = sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}.
A two-sided bound B(A; l, u) means (for every x, l||x||_2 <= ||Ax||_2) and (for every x, ||Ax||_2 <= u||x||_2).
The inverses α^{-1} and β^{-1} and the quotients are ordinary exact real reciprocals and divisions.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every choice of dimensions and real matrices QA, Q, C, and T, and every pair of positive real numbers α and β, assume QA and Q preserve Euclidean norms, C*T equals Q exactly, and T maps R^n onto R^n. Then QA*T has the uniform two-sided Euclidean norm bounds α and β if and only if C has the reciprocal bounds β^{-1} and α^{-1}, respectively. In addition, β/α equals α^{-1}/β^{-1} exactly.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimensions may be zero; no positivity assumption is imposed on m, n, or s.
The theorem is conditional. If any norm-preservation, matrix-equality, positivity, or surjectivity hypothesis is impossible for the supplied data, the implication is vacuously true.
For n > 0, exact norm preservation makes QA and Q injective, so the hypotheses cannot be satisfied when m < n or s < n.
No assumption α <= β is present. The conclusion is an equivalence of bound predicates, not an assertion that either predicate actually holds.
When n = 0, the vector domain contains only the zero vector, so all stated norm inequalities reduce to 0 <= 0 independently of their bound constants.
Surjectivity is asserted only for the matrix-vector map induced by T. An inverse matrix, injectivity, determinant, or nonsingularity is not explicitly mentioned.
QA and Q are required only to preserve the Euclidean norm; orthogonality, square shape, and any particular entrywise structure are not explicitly encoded.
C is not assumed to preserve norms or to be surjective; its only matrix hypothesis is C*T = Q.
Strict positivity of α and β ensures their reciprocals and all displayed quotients have nonzero denominators.
All equalities and inequalities are exact statements over real numbers; no floating-point arithmetic, approximation, error term, or rounding model is encoded.
